patch.value: Typed parameter binding manifests: declare preset parameters once, resolve across settings, templates and seeds

From the 2026-10-21 fleet backlog audit item 2. Declare required preset parameters once in a typed manifest and resolve them consistently through settings, templates and seeds, returning unanswered choices before installation. Acceptance: (1) one supplied project parameter reaches every declared occurrence; (2) unknown/missing bindings refuse before any write; (3) secret values cannot enter generated public seed prose. Deliver typed SDK surface + CLI flags, compact TOON/JSON output, typed refusals with remedies, docs, property tests and real-data validation on a read-only copy of a public fleet tracker in a non-git temp dir.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Overlap check (re-run 2026-10-27 against pm CLI 2026.10.20 SDK and sibling packages): (a) pm-cli SDK has no parameter/interpolation capability — grep over the installed SDK declarations shows settings mutations are literal audited patches (mutateWorkspaceSettings), templates are literal option maps (loadCreateTemplateOptions/runTemplatesShow), client.create takes literal fields; no 'parameter|interpolat|substitut' matches in templates/workspace-contracts/schema declarations. (b) gh search issues --repo unbraind/pm-cli 'parameter binding'/'preset parameter'/'template parameter': no open upstream work. (c) Fleet sibling scan (src/docs) for parameter-binding/interpolation features: no hits. (d) In-package status: presets accept only a few CLI overrides (--prefix, --force, --dry-run, --replace, --with-seeds) and upgrades of known settings; seed and template values are static literals. Conclusion: no overlap — this adds parameter propagation as an explicit authoring contract while the resolved native fields are still validated by the existing core path (preset validation + the host's audited settings mutation), so no core schema change is required.

value.text: Re-review round 1 fixes (2026-10-27) — all five blocking findings addressed class-wide, each with an adversarial test that fails on behavioural revert: (1) SECRETS NEVER ENTER EMITTED OUTPUT: the dry-run patch dump and BOTH sides of every diff settings entry now redact resolved secret values via one primitive (redactSecretValues); summary lines were already redacted; read surfaces (show/list) keep secret occurrences authored because declaration mode never resolves secrets; the ONLY place a secret lands is the private settings.json an apply writes. Revert proof: removing the dry-run dump redaction fails 'dry-run apply redacts secret values from every emitted line'; removing the diff redaction fails 'diff results redact secret values on both sides'. (2) DECLARATIONS BEFORE ANSWERS: catalog/read surfaces resolve leniently (collectParameterValues) and never refuse for unanswered parameters (views flag unanswered, authored occurrences survive); apply and the parameterized diff preview keep strict refusals with the typed remedy; the unified apply now passes supplied values into the definition lookup, so --param answers questions instead of being ignored. Revert proof: restoring strict catalog resolution fails 6 tests (projection, show-with-unanswered, apply-with-param, seed pre-validation, boundary). (3) VALIDATE BEFORE ANY SIDE EFFECT: the unified apply resolves the preset id, every parameter AND the seed bindings at ONE boundary (resolvePresetApplication) before the setup handler runs; a malformed or secret seed binding refuses with settings and templates untouched. Revert proof: restoring post-handler validation fails both seed pre-write tests. (4) RESOLVE ONCE, THREAD EVERYWHERE: apply reads flags/params file exactly once, then threads the effective values through the handler (contextWithResolvedParameters) and into seed creation; applyPreset re-validates injected values (assertResolvedParameterValues) instead of re-reading input. Revert proof: restoring the re-read in the handler fails the injection and boundary tests. (5) CONSISTENT MULTI-PART WRITES: real applies hold a workspace-scoped O_EXCL lock (locks/pm-presets-apply.lock, owner token, stale steal, poll-then-refuse) across the audited settings mutation AND the template writes; dry-runs skip the lock (read-only trackers keep failing only on host locks); release deletes only a file that still carries the owner's token. Revert proof: removing the lock fails the held-lock serialization test (and the concurrent property test now asserts FULL consistency: surviving templates describe the same invocation as the surviving id_prefix). Also wrapped stack plan parameter refusals... removed again as unreachable — stack's candidates loop runs before its try block, so bundled-seed parameter refusals already surface as typed ParameterRefusals; no unreachable wrap shipped.

value.text: Class design: a token comparison followed by unlink is still a TOCTOU race. Every apply now holds a unique immutable admission claim across the existing token-file publication, stale recovery, settings/templates mutation and release. Contenders withdraw before waiting; recovery deletes only the exact observed dead claim pathname, never a shared replacement pathname. The claims directory is retained to avoid directory-generation ABA. Automatic recovery requires matching verified kernel/PID namespace and a PID proven absent; live or unverifiable owners fail closed, including long-running applies. This preserves the existing token-file protocol and every old assertion. All public JSON artifact readers now share descriptor-bound regular-file reads with byte limits; params maps I/O faults to invalid_params_file/exit 2 and upgrade/plan/stack keep their existing typed refusals. Both paramsFile and params-file SDK spellings use that single boundary. Focused tests cover every open/stat/read/close fault, file growth/short reads, descriptor cleanup, all setup/apply/diff entry points, and deterministic cross-process stale/release interleavings paused immediately before unlink.
